paragraphs: Quilltale is a text adventure powered by an AI Game Master that maintains a persistent, structured model of the game world. The story is generated by a language model. The facts are enforced by code.

Most AI games let the model hallucinate freely. It forgets what happened a few turns ago, invents items that were never there, and contradicts itself without noticing. Quilltale works differently. Every location, item, NPC, and player action is tracked in a formal world model that the AI reads before every response and cannot override. If you leave the dagger on the table, it stays there. If you threaten someone, they remember. If you ask to pick up something that is not in your location, the world rejects it, and the story reflects that reality.
The result is a game that actually holds together over a long session, which turns out to be a significantly harder problem than generating a good story.

repositories.name: Irodori-TTS v4.1 Small MF
repositories.description: 4-step MeanFlow Japanese TTS with voice cloning

paragraphs: Demo for Aratako/Irodori-TTS-v4.1-Small-MF, a Japanese text-to-speech model distilled from Aratako/Irodori-TTS-v4.1-Small with MeanFlow.

The rectified-flow (RF) teacher predicts the instantaneous velocity along the path from noise to audio latents and needs 40 sampling steps. The MeanFlow student learns the average velocity over an interval, so it can take much larger updates: at 4 steps it recovers most of the 40-step teacher's Japanese reading accuracy (JKYB-Parakeet target Kana-CER 7.67% vs 6.88%) and speaker similarity (JVS CAM++ 0.743 vs 0.752 at 30 s of reference), where 4-step RF collapses to 11.10% / 0.384.

Guidance is fused into the teacher targets during distillation, so inference uses one conditional DiT evaluation per step and there are no CFG knobs — CFG scales, Sway Sampling, noise truncation and speaker-KV scaling are all ignored for MeanFlow checkpoints.

Style captions — describe the voice, emotion and delivery in Japanese.
Zero-shot voice cloning — upload one or more reference clips (concatenated, up to 120 s).
Emoji style controls — insert control emoji (whisper, sigh, giggle, …) inline in the text.

repositories.name: Krea 2 Turbo BBox
repositories.description: Layout-controlled comics with a draggable bbox canvas

paragraphs: Demo of jimmycarter/krea2-turbo-bbox — a Krea 2 finetune merged with the Turbo distillation delta (8 steps, no CFG).

The model was trained on a compact grounding DSL that places panels, characters, objects and verbatim text into explicit [x0,y0,x1,y1] boxes on a 0–1000 grid. This Space exposes that DSL directly and wraps it in a draggable box canvas: the canvas and the prompt textbox are two views of the same string, so moving a box rewrites its coordinates and editing the text redraws the canvas.

Example prompts span realistic photography (product shots, portraits, multi-subject scenes, landscapes), posters/typography, and multi-panel comics, plus plain-prose prompts — showing that the bbox layout control applies to any subject matter, not just comics.
